clue.text: Legendary vessel impounded by Japanese navy is Greek

indicators.note: to be impounded by something is to be shut up inside it, so the vessel sits within the other letters

parts.note: the Argo was the ship of Jason and the Argonauts in Greek legend

explanation.surface: A mythical ship seized by Japan's navy turns out to be Greek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek' looks like a description of the ship, but it is the definition, as in 'it's all Greek to me'.
explanation.definitionFit: Unintelligible specialist language is described as Greek, from the idiom 'it's all Greek to me'.

clue.text: I'm surprised dons love cheeky part of theatrical ensemble

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

indicators.note: to don is to put on, so the exclamation is worn inside the other letters

parts.note: pert means cheeky or impudent
aha is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: Someone is shocked that academic dons enjoy a saucy bit of theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ensemble' means an outfit of clothes, not a group of performers; 'dons' looks like university teachers but is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A collapsible top hat was worn to the opera as part of formal evening dress.

clue.text: Let It Be recording stolen from seven-piece band

indicators.note: something stolen from a word is taken away from it

parts.note: a septet is a group of seven musicians
an EP, an extended play, is a short record

explanation.surface: A Beatles song is pinched from a seven-strong group's set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let It Be' is the Beatles title on the surface, but here it is the proofreader's instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Proofreaders mark a deleted word to be restored with this Latin instruction meaning 'let it stand'.

clue.text: Nearly meet suspect linked to lead?

definitions.note: an adjective: relating to a chemical element such as lead

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious, so these letters are not to be trusted in their order

explanation.surface: A near-meeting with a suspect connected to a police lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' reads as a police clue, but it is the metal with symbol Pb; the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead is a chemical element, so anything to do with it is, in the chemist's sense, of an element.

clue.text: Stick man ending in perpendicular lines

indicators.note: to line something is to sit inside it, so the letter goes within the chess term

parts.note: a man in chess or draughts is a piece

indicators.note: the ending of the word perpendicular is its final letter

explanation.surface: A stick figure is drawn with lines ending at right angles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick man' reads as one phrase, but 'Stick' alone is the definition and 'man' is a chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick a knife or spike into something is to puncture or stab it through.

clue.text: Long for leader to pre-empt trouble

indicators.note: to pre-empt is to come before, so the leader's letters go in front

parts.note: a head is a leader or chief
to ache for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: Wanting to lead in order to head off trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A source of persistent worry or difficulty is called a pain in the head, figuratively.

clue.text: Support upset about aggressive environment

parts.note: to bear is to support a weight

indicators.note: about signals turning round, so the word for upset is read backwards

parts.note: to tip is to upset or overturn

explanation.surface: A supporter angry about a hostile atmosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a pit for baiting bears, figuratively any hostile, combative setting such as a rowdy parliament.

clue.text: Unfair wager in which he blew lot stupidly

indicators.note: the phrase says the wager holds the following letters within it

parts.note: a bet is a wager

indicators.note: done stupidly means done in a muddled way, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A dodgy bet on which a gambler foolishly lost a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stupidly' jumbles HE BLEW LOT into ELOWTHEBEL, which 'in which' places between B and ET.
explanation.definitionFit: From boxing, where a punch below the waistline breaks the rules; hence any dishonourable tactic.

clue.text: Be slow to introduce sex to role playing

indicators.note: introducing one thing to another puts it inside, so the sex appeal goes within
playing about with letters rearranges them

parts.note: IT is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: Dragging one's feet about adding a sex scene to a part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges the four letters into LOER; 'sex' is IT, old slang for sex appeal, which 'introduce' puts in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To dawdle or hang about aimlessly is to take one's time rather than hurry along.

clue.text: Crowded around men pursuing partisan

definitions.note: an adjective here: biased, as is one whose mind is already made up

indicators.note: around says the first word wraps itself about the second

parts.note: pressed means crowded or pushed together
a posse is a band of men in pursuit of a fugitive

explanation.surface: A mob surrounding a group chasing a resistance fighter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partisan' looks like a guerrilla being chased, but it is the adjective meaning biased.
explanation.definitionFit: One whose opinion is already formed in someone's favour is biased, not impartial.

clue.text: Auditor's recording device beat something to simplify calculation

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so the words are as heard

parts.note: a logger is a device that records data, and a rhythm is a beat

explanation.surface: An accountant's tape recorder thumps out a figure that eases the sums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' suggests an accountant but means a hearer; LOGGER RHYTHM, said in a non-rhotic British accent, matches the mathematical term.
explanation.definitionFit: Tables of these exponents turned multiplication into addition, easing arithmetic before calculators.

clue.text: Free beer regularly included in performer's list of requirements

parts.note: to rid is to free of something

indicators.note: taking letters regularly means every other one

explanation.surface: A pop star demands free beer in the dressing room.
explanation.definitionFit: Touring artists attach a contract appendix listing backstage demands, famously such as bowls of sweets.

clue.text: Crank about to be placed in secure hospital

indicators.note: the short word is put inside the others

parts.note: to win is to secure or gain
C, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: An eccentric about to be locked up in a secure psychiatric hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crank' reads as an eccentric person, but here it is the verb or noun for turning a handle.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoist is worked by turning a handle, so to wind up with one is to crank.

clue.text: New College blocking fees to improve on fool's mark

indicators.note: blocking something means standing in the way, inside it

parts.note: dues are fees
to cap is to better or outdo

explanation.surface: A new college stands in the way of higher tuition fees.
explanation.definitionFit: A conical hat was once put on a slow pupil as a badge of stupidity.

clue.text: Labour leader's penetrating treacherous parting glance

indicators.note: the leader's letter penetrates, going into the longer word

parts.note: defection is deserting one's side for the enemy

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: The Labour leader cuts through a traitor's farewell look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'glance' looks like a look, but is a ball or blow glancing off something.
explanation.definitionFit: A glancing blow is turned aside off its course, which is what a deviation of path means.

clue.text: Classic book by Forster has naked swimming

indicators.note: letters swimming move about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: E.M. Forster wrote a classic in which a character swims naked.
explanation.walkthrough: Forster is a plausible author of a classic, but the book is by Joseph Conrad.
explanation.definitionFit: Conrad's 1899 novella of a journey up the Congo is a standard classic of English literature.

clue.text: Uninhibited singer with style that's lacking in control

indicators.note: read as un-inhibited, the bird loses its outer letters, its constraints

parts.note: a canary is a songbird
chic means style or elegance

explanation.surface: A free-spirited vocalist whose flair lacks discipline.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawless and disorderly, as with a state without government or restraint.

clue.text: Son practised reversing in car that's a banger

indicators.note: in places these letters inside the car maker's name

parts.note: Kia is a Korean car make

indicators.note: reversing turns the letters backwards, as a car reverses

parts.note: able means skilled, practised

explanation.surface: A son practising reversing in an old car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banger' is British slang both for a clapped-out car, as the surface suggests, and for a sausage, which is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A kielbasa is a smoked Polish sausage, and banger is British slang for a sausage.

clue.text: Helps case for atheism by tempering irreverent behaviour

indicators.note: tempering a mixture works it into a new state, so the letters are rearranged
the case of a word is its outside letters

explanation.surface: An argument for atheism is aided by moderating disrespectful conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case for' takes A and M from atheism; 'tempering' shuffles HELPS, AM and BY.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking or acting with contempt for God or sacred things is profanity.

clue.text: Corporation starts to acquire technology of chip producer

parts.note: corporation is old slang for a pot belly

indicators.note: the starts of the following words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A company begins acquiring a microchip maker's technology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' and 'chip' suggest computing, but a corporation is a paunch and a chip is a fried potato.
explanation.definitionFit: Chips, British for fries, are cut from this tuber, so it is the vegetable source of them.

clue.text: Blot out recollection of Caesarean section

indicators.note: read as re-collection, the letters are gathered back the other way round
a section is a piece cut from inside the word

explanation.surface: Wiping out the memory of a caesarean birth.
explanation.definitionFit: To expunge or obliterate, as one removes ink with a rubber.

clue.text: Foreign places lowering resistance on ship

indicators.note: in a down entry lowering a letter moves it further down

parts.note: abroad as a noun means foreign parts
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Overseas, the resistance on a ship is being lowered.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on a vessel is to be on deck, as passengers are once they embark.

clue.text: Soliciting publicity explicitly in each case is legitimate

indicators.note: the same letters sit inside every one of the three words

explanation.surface: Openly drumming up publicity for oneself is lawful.
explanation.walkthrough: The same five letters appear inside each of the three words, which is what 'in each case' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawful or permitted, the opposite of illicit.

clue.text: Gloomy rendition of sober tune

indicators.note: a rendition is a fresh performance, so the letters are arranged anew

explanation.surface: A dirge-like performance of a solemn melody.
explanation.definitionFit: A literary word for dark or shadowy, from Latin tenebrae, darkness.

clue.text: Dawning of new era could be at hand

indicators.note: the dawning of a word is its first letter
could be signals an alternative arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: The dawn of a new age may be imminent.
explanation.definitionFit: Close by or imminent, in place or time.

clue.text: Restaurant's first to open branch and last to go

indicators.note: the ordinal is placed to open up the abbreviation, inside it

parts.note: BR is an abbreviation for branch
1st, the ordinal, looks like IST

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A restaurant chain's first branch opens and its last closes.
explanation.walkthrough: '1st' is written as IST, the digit one read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A small, informal French-style eatery serving simple meals.

clue.text: Confident Trump's behind rude outburst

parts.note: an American such as Trump calls the backside the ass

indicators.note: a burst word has its letters blown apart and reassembled

explanation.surface: A self-assured Trump stands behind an offensive outburst.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' looks like support, but is the bottom, in American English an ass.
explanation.definitionFit: Sure of oneself, poised and self-possessed.
